lesson.menu_title: Countdown to Burnaby — The First 48 Hours
lesson.menu_desc: Landing, meeting the host family and asking the questions back -- 36 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 1 -- Countdown to Burnaby: The First 48 Hours
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Laís Paludetto Rodrigues | Lesson 1 -- Countdown to Burnaby

listenings.text: Hey Lais, it's Greg, your host dad in Burnaby. I know you're probably still packing, so I'll keep this short. We'll be waiting for you right outside the doors at international arrivals, and I'll have a sign with your name on it, so don't panic if the airport looks huge. It's about a forty minute drive from the airport to our place in Burnaby, and Emma, our daughter, is coming with me because she refuses to miss it. One thing about the weather: everybody tells you Vancouver is freezing, but in September it's actually pretty mild, so bring a light jacket for the first weeks. Have a safe flight and text us when you land.

Good morning, this is a message for our new international students from the district welcome office. Congratulations on getting here. Your first appointment is orientation, and it happens on Monday at nine in the main hall, not in the classroom building, so give yourself extra time to find it. Please bring your passport and the letter from your school in Brazil. After orientation you'll get your timetable and a student card, and somebody from the buddy programme will walk you around the building. If you feel lost in the first week, that is completely normal. Every single one of us felt exactly the same. Just ask. People here are used to it and nobody minds explaining twice.

extra_audio.text: Greg finds Lais outside the arrivals doors and introduces himself. Lais says she is happy to be there and asks how long the drive is. Greg explains that Burnaby is about forty minutes away. Lais asks who else lives in the house. Greg says his daughter Emma is in the car waiting for them.

items.situation: You land in Vancouver. The officer at passport control asks why you are in Canada. Answer him and say how long you are staying.
tips: I'm going to study at ... high school.

items.situation: Your host dad is driving you home. You want to know who else lives in the house. Ask him.
tips: Do you have any other kids?

items.situation: Somebody at the door says a long sentence and you catch about half of it. Ask them to repeat it, politely.
tips: Sorry, could you say that again?
I didn't catch that last part.
Could you speak a little more slowly, please?

items.situation: A student in the hall asks where you are from. Answer, and then ask her something back so the conversation does not die.
tips: I'm from Sao Paulo, in Brazil.
How about you? Are you from Burnaby?
How long have you been at this school?

items.situation: You are jet lagged and you need to know what time breakfast happens in this house. Ask your host mum.
tips: What time do you usually have breakfast?
Should I wake up at a certain time?
Is it okay if I sleep in tomorrow?

items.situation: Somebody uses a word you have never heard. Ask what it means without pretending you understood.
tips: I've never heard that word before.
